facts.why: The missing $2 million is the money Virginia took before opening night, not a pool. Siegel lets her keep it. Funding began at $1 million and the cost rose past $6 million.

facts.text: The boss's diction drill: "Six slick ships sail south."
facts.why: No diction drill or tongue twister appears in the transcript, Wikipedia or Wikiquote. Siegel does tell reporters his name is Benjamin, as in the Bible.
facts.fix: The boss on his name: “My name is Benjamin, as in the Bible.”

facts.text: Miss Hill's way: gin, fresh lime and soda, shell left in.
facts.why: The transcript has no gin rickey or any cocktail scene for Virginia, only talk of phoney champagne in a club. Reworded as a plain drink for her.
facts.fix: A drink for Virginia: gin, fresh lime and soda, shell left in.

facts.text: Our namesake, hung in the lobby. Long legs, all pink,
facts.full: Our namesake, hung in the lobby. Long legs, all pink, and about as native to the desert as we are.
facts.why: The film never shows a flamingo picture in a lobby. It does have Siegel say he will name the hotel the Flamingo after Virginia, so the namesake line stands.
facts.fix: Our namesake, Virginia's nickname. Long legs, all pink,

vibe.verdict: A pink, period Flamingo invite with the right budget gag, though the food is just forties supper club and a few lines are guesses.
